relationships.subject: HDAC2
relationships.evidence_quote: Thus, our findings reveal that HDAC2 functions as a pivotal transcriptional repressor of neuropathic pain via constitutively suppressing α2δ-1 expression and ensuing presynaptic NMDA receptor activity in the spinal cord.

relationships.subject: α2δ-1
relationships.evidence_quote: Excess α2δ-1 proteins produced after nerve injury directly interact with glutamate NMDA receptors to potentiate synaptic NMDA receptor activity in the spinal cord, a prominent mechanism of nerve pain.

key_findings: Nerve injury reduces HDAC2 (not HDAC3) enrichment at the Cacna2d1 promoter in DRG, raising histone acetylation and α2δ-1.
Hdac2 knockdown/knockout in DRG neurons causes lasting mechanical hypersensitivity reversed by NMDAR block or gabapentin.
